items.title: Slack alerting + multi-channel notify (and the recursion incident)
items.verified:
notify.sh now supports SLACK via chat.postMessage with SLACK_BOT_TOKEN (Gray Reserve has a bot token + 23 channel ids, NOT a webhook; webhook kept as fallback). Severity routing: failures -> SLACK_CHANNEL_ERRORS, everything else -> SLACK_CHANNEL/SLACK_CHANNEL_PROSPECTING. Slack answers HTTP 200 with {"ok":false} on auth/channel errors so the response is parsed for '"ok":true' rather than trusting the status code. NOTIFY_CHANNEL accepts a comma-separated list. Jeff set NOTIFY_CHANNEL=telegram,slack and both channels confirmed delivering.

INCIDENT 2026-08-15 - EXPONENTIAL ALERT LOOP, MY BUG. The first fan-out re-invoked the script as `NOTIFY_CHANNEL=telegram "$0" ...`. notify.sh SOURCES .env near the top, so the child re-read .env, got `telegram,slack` back, and fanned out again - each level spawning two more. Hundreds of Telegram messages reached Jeff's phone before it was stopped. Killing notify.sh alone did NOT work: the PARENT shell kept spawning fresh children, so the parent pid had to be killed first.

FIX: fan-out now passes NOTIFY_FORCE_CHANNEL, a name .env never defines, so sourcing cannot clobber it; the child sees one channel, does not match the *,*) branch, and recursion terminates after one level. A load-bearing comment at that code describes the incident so the guard is not removed later as redundant. VERIFIED with a stubbed curl that counts invocations: exactly 2 (one telegram, one slack) and the process terminates - a regression shows as a rising count instead of a flood on a phone.

LESSON, generalisable: an env var passed parent->child does NOT survive when the child re-sources its own config - the config always wins. Any parent->child signal must use a name the config never sets. The `claude --bg` pipeline pool passes state to children the same way.

items.title: FORK BOMB (not this lane): scripts/notify.sh self-recursed 3,530 deep and exhausted the machine's process table
items.verified:
FIXED + regression-tested 2026-08-15. Root cause was NOT a second path into the fan-out; the reported 'second path' was never reproduced and the fan-out is correct. The live defect was that the NOTIFY_DEPTH backstop was INERT: read, sanitised, compared (-gt 1) and exported, but NEVER INCREMENTED, so every process in a chain exported 0 and the guard could not fire at any depth. Proven by tracing NOTIFY_DEPTH at each level of a real fan-out against a credential-stripped copy of the live .env - parent and both children all logged DEPTH=[0].

FIX: NOTIFY_DEPTH=$((NOTIFY_DEPTH + 1)) on ENTRY (before any channel logic), exported, refusing above 2 with exit 3. Sited at entry, not at the fan-out, so it bounds recursion arriving through ANY path - including a cycle that never touches the fan-out (the email branch shells out to gmail.py). Caps total processes at 1 + number_of_channels regardless of which conditional fix is later reintroduced. exit 3 is deliberate and safe: db.py::_notify uses check=False, the fan-out uses || true, outreach-notify-simple.sh uses || exit 0.

ELIMINATED BY EVIDENCE (not argument): db.py::_notify passes an ABSOLUTE path and has no retry loop; exactly one "$0" self-invocation site exists; only one notify.sh on the machine has a fan-out and it carries the guard (pristine/ and .klaudius/base/ have no fan-out at all); no Claude hook references notify.sh; .env is byte-clean with no trailing/doubled comma. Real .env fan-out terminates at exactly 3 processes, depth 2.

TEST: tests/test_notify_recursion.py, 9 assertions, all passing. Asserts the contract (NOTIFY_CHANNEL=a,b,c -> exactly 3 sends at depth 2) AND deliberately reintroduces the original defect in a throwaway copy to prove the counter contains it anyway. Senders stubbed via a fake curl on PATH (nothing leaves the machine); children run under RLIMIT_NPROC=current+25 in their own process group so a regression dies with EAGAIN and is reaped with killpg instead of reproducing the outage. Mutation-tested: removing the increment fails 5/9, removing the export fails 5/9.

LESSON: a guard that cannot fire is worse than no guard - it reads as covered in review, which is exactly why the second incident was not caught. Assert that a guard FIRES, never merely that it exists.

Its useEffect was keyed [seed] only, so ScrollTriggers were built for the FIRST route loaded and never again, while the persistent rule html[data-motion=ready] [data-reveal]{opacity:0} kept applying to every route after it. Tapping a menu link therefore produced a hero, a permanent white void and a footer. A direct URL load of the same route was perfect, the route returned 200, and the copy was present in the DOM — which is why it passed every earlier check. REPRODUCED on the live site in mobile WebKit before the fix: soft nav to /about left 8 of 9 [data-reveal] sections at opacity 0 and scrolling did not clear them.

SiteNav owns its own scrolled state (the data-[scrolled=false] pattern matched NEITHER class when Motion had not run, leaving the header with no background at all) and is opaque whenever the mobile menu is open. SiteChat: launcher lifts above any [data-sticky-bottom] bar (measured via ResizeObserver) and clears env(safe-area-inset-bottom); [data-chat-gutter] on the footer's last row reserves the corner; the open panel is a full-screen sheet below 640px with its own close button; the input is 16px so iOS stops auto-zooming. VERIFIED LIVE, screenshots viewed: both sites, / /about /services, 1440x900 chromium AND 375x812 mobile WebKit, every subpage reached by SOFT NAVIGATION after a 20s linger. [data-reveal] elements still at opacity<0.05 after a full scroll: 0 of 0 on all 12 route/viewport/site combinations. Nav background rgb(28,25,23) with the menu open (was rgba(0,0,0,0)). items.title: CRITICAL: shared-lane publish breaks React hydration — EVERY klaudius site ships with no working JS
notes: 2026-08-16, found by chasing Jeff's 'no motion on my cell' and 'chat bubble doesn't open'. Both are ONE fault, and it is not a design problem. PROOF, same build, two servers: local out/ served with python http.server -> reactHydrated TRUE, lenis class present, data-motion attr set. Same bytes published through the shared lane -> reactHydrated FALSE, no react keys on any element, no lenis, no data-motion. So the BUILD is fine and the PUBLISH/SERVE layer breaks it. MECHANISM: Next static export hardcodes /_next/ paths at build time. publish-klaudius-tenant.mjs serves the tenant under /klaudius/<slug>/ and REWRITES asset URLs afterwards — including inside the RSC flight payload, which is measurable: the inline __next_f script grows from 43,038 bytes locally to 44,046 served, purely from injected path prefixes. The <script src> tags then resolve (all chunks return 200, verified) but Next's runtime still expects its build-time /_next/ paths, so hydration bails SILENTLY — no console error, no visible failure, just a dead page. IMPACT: every prospect site on *.grayreserve.agency has no chat and no motion, i.e. two of the things the $98/mo is sold on, and it would have shipped to real owners. Contrast, richness and ship-scan all PASS on such a page because they read static HTML/CSS. FIX DIRECTION (not applied — needs a decision): build each tenant WITH basePath/assetPrefix set to '/klaudius/<slug>' in next.config.mjs so the paths are correct at build time and nothing is rewritten. Alternative: serve each tenant from its own path root. Post-hoc rewriting cannot work. GATE TO ADD REGARDLESS: the QA/deploy pass must assert hydration on the LIVE url — Object.keys(el).some(k=>k.startsWith('__react')) — because every existing gate passes on a dead page.
items.verified: FIXED 2026-08-16. Root cause: the publisher's rewriteAssetUrls() was rewriting paths INSIDE Next's inline `self.__next_f.push(...)` RSC payload. That payload carries the module identifiers React uses to resolve client components at hydration; they LOOK like paths, so a blanket URL rewrite mangled them — measurably, the inline script grew 43,038 -> 44,046 bytes. Result was a SILENT hydration failure: every chunk returned 200, the page rendered from static HTML, but React never attached (no __react keys, no motion, chat would not open) with `Minified React error #412` in console. FIX: split the document, protect inline non-src <script> blocks behind placeholders, rewrite only real markup, restore untouched. VERIFIED: local and served inline payloads now match EXACTLY at 43,542 bytes, and a real browser on the LIVE url reports reactHydrated=true, lenis=true, data-motion='ready'. NOTE assetPrefix was NOT the fix — I tried that first and it changed nothing.

It doubled from ~25 min because the 2026-08-16 design lift added generated volume per page AND the route decision chose 14 routes (home, services, 3 per-service, about, contact, blog + 5 articles, privacy, terms) at --effort high. Fable's ranked plan, in order: (1) ~6-9 min: move derivable structure into templates/trade-site -- sitemap/robots/llms.txt routes, schema.ts, both blog renderers, nav/footer/layout are ~700-900 lines of ZERO design content retyped every build; make them read site-data.ts (add a ROUTES export) so the model authors only data + design pages. Writes drop 30 -> ~18. No design risk. (2) ~5-8 min: delegate the 5 blog articles (~4,000 words of pure prose, no design surface) to ONE subagent concurrent with page writing. REQUIRES amending app/CLAUDE.md Critical Rule 10 explicitly -- do not sneak it. Main session still reviews against anti-ai-slop before committing to blog-data.ts. (3) ~3-4 min: cut seed blog 5 -> 3 articles on SPEC builds, backfill at conversion via /seo. Fallback if (2) is refused, not stacked on top. (4) ~2-4 min: --effort is PROCESS-WIDE on claude -p and cannot vary per stage. But skills carry effort: frontmatter (build/qa-fix say high, seo says medium), so dispatch at --effort medium and let build's own frontmatter carry the design stage. MUST VERIFY FIRST that skill-frontmatter effort beats the CLI flag in this Claude Code version. (5) HELD IN RESERVE, do not take yet: parallel route generation (~10-15 min). Palette and component duplication are well contained by tokens + deterministic gates, but cross-page composition drift is NOT -- image-role uniqueness is per-SITE and a per-page subagent cannot see its siblings' choices. Only take it if a measured post-change build still exceeds 35 min, and only with a main-session image-role manifest as the coordination artifact. REJECTED: cutting per-service pages (buying-intent lane, Jeff personally flagged their absence); anything trading richness/motion/section-treatment floors for speed (that is how you get a FAST 2/10); dropping to sonnet for build (design quality is the one thing no gate can catch).

items.title: dispatch-build.sh watchdog killed every healthy build
items.verified: FIXED and verified 2026-08-16. BSD find (macOS) does NOT parse relative -newermt strings: it returns zero matches and exit 0, a silent fail-open. Measured: ten consecutive `find clients -type f -newermt '5 minutes ago'` returned 0 while `find ... -mmin -5` returned 630 on the same tree at the same instant. The watchdog's liveness probe was built on -newermt '90 seconds ago', so sig was permanently '0', last_change never advanced, and it would have KILLED EVERY HEALTHY BUILD at the 8-minute stall threshold while reporting a stall that never happened -- a watchdog manufacturing the failure it exists to catch. Switched to -mmin -2 (whole minutes only). Also removed a tangled condition whose second clause could never change the outcome and which disguised the bug. VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS: against the live running build the new probe read 22 while the old read 0; against a synthetic tree with only a 09:00 file the probe read 0, and 1 after one fresh write. bash -n clean.

items.title: The 'hang' since build 3 was QA subagents, not a hang
items.verified:
Jeff has read every build since build 3 as hanging. It never was. A parent Claude session writes NOTHING to its own transcript for the entire time a sub-agent runs, and QA runs as a sub-agent for 10-16 minutes per round. From outside that is indistinguishable from death: silent process, flat transcript, 0.0% CPU, no new client files while the reviewer reads screenshots.
It fooled ME TWICE in one session. First `ps | grep 'claude -p'` found nothing because the child appears as bare `claude`, and I told Jeff the process was 'gone entirely' — wrong. Then I watched the parent transcript freeze for 5 minutes and was about to call it hung, when the work was happening in <session>/subagents/*.jsonl the whole time.
MEASURED on abacus: QA = 26.6 min of an 84-min build (32%) — round 1 10.6 min, round 2 16.0 min, round 3 also ran, plus 3.9 min across TWO auto-compaction events. The compactions are caused by screenshots: the reviewer's context held 21 image blocks = 2.74 MB = 89.4% of everything in it (tool output 0.30 MB, text 0.03 MB).
SHIPPED: (a) scripts/build-status.sh — one command answering 'working or stuck?' from the UNION of client-file writes, parent transcript AND subagent transcripts, because each signal alone has a blind spot. Live-tested against the running build. Note it must avoid mapfile/readarray — macOS ships bash 3.2 — which the first version got wrong and running it caught. (b) scripts/shrink-screenshots.mjs — PNG->WebP q88 before the reviewer reads them. Settings are deliberately conservative after Jeff pushed back on an earlier 900px/q72 draft: format conversion is where nearly all the saving is, downscaling is what destroys evidence, so desktop resizes only to 1280 and MOBILE IS NEVER RESIZED. Pixel-level checks (contrast, fonts, gallery void) read the live page and never these files, which is why compressing them is safe. (c) qa-reviewer.md now says write findings PER ROUTE as you go — a compaction mid-review can otherwise discard images before the findings were written down, which is a correctness bug wearing a performance costume.
⚠️ Fable caught that I had created shrink-screenshots.mjs and WIRED IT NOWHERE — the orphaned-scorer failure already in my own memory index. Now called from qa-reviewer Step 3, and the reviewer is told the files are .webp and to `ls` rather than hard-code an extension.

items.title: Scoped round-2+ QA with double-keyed escalation (Fable's design) - SHIPPED
items.note:
Fable's biggest QA lever, ~10-12 min/build, but it is GATED ON QA-01 SHIPPING FIRST and QA-01's gate proving itself on a real build.
THE EVIDENCE AGAINST THE NAIVE VERSION IS ALREADY IN: on abacus, qa-fix's round-1 change was a one-character JSX fix on /about. A scoped round 2 that reviewed 'the page qa-fix touched plus the deterministic gates' would have re-reviewed /about, passed, and SHIPPED THE HORROR CLOWN — which round 1 missed and which lived on the home page. So round 2's disproportionate full re-review functioned as a second lottery ticket and it won.
Fable's design replaces that luck with mechanism: round 2 still runs as a FRESH agent (CLAUDE.md's independence mandate is preserved — scoping the work is not self-review), but its scope needs TWO keys to both say 'local': (1) the reviewer tags each critical LOCAL or SYSTEMIC in the report; (2) the PARENT measures qa-fix's actual footprint via a shasum snapshot before/after — never the fixer's self-report, because a fixer that touched globals.css while 'fixing a space' is exactly the case that must escalate. Full re-review is mandatory if the real diff touches globals.css, layout.tsx, tailwind/next config, anything under _components/ (incl. blog-data.ts), or any public/ file used by >1 route; or any deterministic gate failed; or a structural critical was found; or the diff exceeds the routes the LOCAL tags named.
A scoped round still re-runs GLOBALLY: next build + the whole deterministic battery (font, contrast, tokens, ship-scan, richness, PHOTO_CHECK, route status, word counts, titles) — those are scripts, ~2-3 min, and cover every page regardless of scope. Then screenshots of the changed route(s) PLUS ONE ROTATING UNCHANGED CANARY route, which is the deliberate replacement for the lottery-ticket effect.
DO NOT scope round 1, ever — it is the only full look the site gets, and abacus proves even a full look misses things.

LIVE EVIDENCE 2026-08-16 from the-woodlands-plumbing-and-air (the HyperUI experiment build): investigated an 80+ minute, 10M+ token overrun that Jeff correctly suspected was NOT the HyperUI reference set (confirmed: only 3 of 111 Read calls touched anything hyperui-related -- it read INDEX.md once and essentially never opened a component file). The real driver: every deterministic gate ran multiple times across the build -- verify-photos.mjs 6x, contrast-check.mjs and font-check.mjs 5x each, richness-check.mjs 4x, ship-scan/aeo-check/shrink-screenshots 3x each, design-ledger.mjs 2x -- 31 total gate invocations, the signature of multiple full QA rounds each re-running the ENTIRE 8-script battery from scratch. This is also the first build tonight carrying the full combined weight of every gate added tonight (photo vision, convergence ledger, hard-blocker contract, photo treatment) simultaneously -- prior builds never ran under all of them at once. Direct, concrete confirmation that scoping round-2+ QA to the deterministic battery PLUS only the changed files (rather than the full visual re-review AND re-running every gate) is the real lever here, exactly as designed. Minor separate finding from the same investigation: 169 of 215 Bash calls (79%) carried a redundant `export PATH=...` prefix not instructed anywhere in the skills -- real but minor overhead (low thousands of tokens), not the dominant cost.

UNBLOCKED AND SHIPPED 2026-08-16. The stated unblock gate -- 'verify-photos.mjs must run on at least one full real build and be seen to fire (or cleanly pass)' -- is satisfied: it ran across all 3 QA rounds of the-woodlands-plumbing-and-air build 2 tonight and correctly reported PHOTO_CHECK=PASS (10/10 photos cleared) as a real, not-just-didn't-crash verdict. That converts the one defect class scoping would have missed (the abacus horror-clown case) from luck into a deterministic script, exactly the condition Fable's design required before shipping.

Implemented Fable's exact double-keyed design, not a simplified version: CLAUDE.md's QA Loop section rewritten with round 1 unconditionally full (never scoped, ever), and a new 'Round 2+: scoped, double-keyed' section -- pre/post shasum snapshot of the client's source tree around every /qa-fix call (ground truth, never the fixer's self-report), an explicit escalation-trigger list (globals.css/layout.tsx/config/_components/ or a >1-route public/ file/any gate FAIL/any SYSTEMIC tag/any diff outside the reviewer's covered routes forces a full unscoped round), and when no trigger fires: full deterministic battery every round regardless of scope (only ~2-3 min, covers everything) but screenshots/visual review limited to the touched route(s) plus one deterministically-rotating unchanged canary route. qa-reviewer.md updated with the LOCAL/SYSTEMIC tagging convention (default to SYSTEMIC when unsure) and a cross-reference to the mechanism, so a thin future invocation still knows the convention exists even if the orchestrator prompt doesn't fully restate it.

Direct answer to Jeff's cost/time ask: this is the QA-side half of getting build time down -- round 2 and round 3 on tonight's build each paid the FULL ~10-12 min re-review + full gate re-run cost; a scoped round 3 (round 2's fixes were narrow, single-file changes per the qa-fix diffs) would have cost a few minutes instead. Not yet tested end-to-end on a real build -- the next full test run is where this gets proven, alongside the marketing-tier HyperUI floor (HYPERUI-02) and whatever Fable's separate token-efficiency review (dispatched in parallel) surfaces.

items.title: publish-and-serve.sh aliases instead of binding a project domain — every new tenant will 302
items.note:
Found the hard way on abacus-plumbing 2026-08-16. Step 5 of scripts/publish-and-serve.sh runs `vercel alias set <deployment> <host>`. A bare alias does NOT bypass Vercel Deployment Protection, so the hostname 302s to vercel.com/sso-api and the script's own verification step correctly fails. Existing tenants work because their hosts were bound as PROJECT DOMAINS at some point; new ones will not be.
PROOF IT IS THE HOST AND NOT THE DEPLOYMENT: impact-landscapes-frisco.grayreserve.agency and abacus-plumbing.grayreserve.agency were on the SAME deployment (pf9kv1gsq) and returned 200 and 302 respectively.
MANUAL FIX THAT WORKED: `vercel alias rm <host>` (needed first — `domains add` refuses with alias_conflict while an alias exists) then `vercel domains add <host> gr-no-website-builds`. Returned domain_already_assigned and the host served 200 immediately.
THE DURABLE FIX: replace the alias step with a project-domain bind, which also auto-follows future production deploys and would retire the separate re-alias-and-verify dance the script does today. This is the SAME root cause already recorded in OPS-01 (athleteos has no cert because its binding was lost) and OPS-03 (chat.grayreserve.agency is a pinned alias that will not follow the next deploy) — all three are one problem and should be fixed together.
NOTE the ordering constraint for any scripted version: rm-then-add is destructive for a moment, so on a host that is currently SERVING it must be done in the other order or with a health check, otherwise a working tenant blinks out.

items.title: assetPrefix missing -> ROOT CAUSE of dead menu/motion/chat on every affected tenant
items.verified:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-16, root cause of everything Jeff reported this session as 'no motion on my cell', 'chat bubble doesn't open', 'menu doesn't work' -- all ONE bug, not three.
PROVEN BY CONTROLLED BISECTION, not assumed: local build of abacus-plumbing hydrated fine served plainly; served-through-the-lane bytes did not; served bytes were BYTE-IDENTICAL to local once /klaudius/<slug>/ prefixes were normalised (confirmed via python diff, zero real content difference); the ONLY remaining variable was next.config.mjs's assetPrefix. Controlled comparison: demolition-okc HAD assetPrefix and hydrated; abacus-plumbing had none and did not. Next bakes the asset base into the client runtime at BUILD TIME, so a build with none ships a runtime that requests its own chunks from the subdomain ROOT while assets live under /klaudius/<slug>/ -- React never resolves its client components and never hydrates.
WHY IT LOOKED LIKE A DESIGN BUG FOR AN ENTIRE SESSION: fails completely silently. Page renders from static HTML, every chunk still 200s, zero console errors (a module never requested can't throw). Symptom set: dead mobile menu, chat bubble that will not open, no GSAP/Lenis, every [data-reveal] frozen at opacity 1.
⚠️ CORRECTS A PRIOR ENTRY IN THIS SAME REPO: an earlier note claimed 'assetPrefix was NOT the hydration fix... deployed it, changed nothing' -- that note was wrong, almost certainly tested without a full rebuild (Next only bakes assetPrefix in at build time, so testing against a stale build would show no change and look like a dead end).
TWO LIVE TENANTS WERE AFFECTED: abacus-plumbing and impact-landscapes-frisco (found by auditing every client's next.config.mjs for the flag -- 4 of 6 clients were missing it, though 2 of those 4 are scratch/smoke-test dirs, not real tenants).
FIXED STRUCTURALLY so it cannot regress: templates/trade-site/next.config.mjs now DERIVES assetPrefix from the client directory name (basename(dirname(siteDir)) -> /klaudius/<slug>) instead of requiring anyone to remember to set it -- a value someone has to remember is a value that eventually is not set, which is exactly what happened. Escape hatch: KLAUDIUS_ASSET_PREFIX='' opts out explicitly for a tenant served from its own project root.
DOCUMENTED in .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md with the full failure signature and a one-line verification command (grep -c '"/_next/static' out/index.html must be 0).
VERIFIED END TO END on production https://abacus-plumbing.grayreserve.agency/ after redeploy: React hydrated=true (real __react fiber on the menu button), mobile drawer opens on click (aria-expanded flips true, drawer mounts in DOM) when isolated from unrelated prefetch noise, [data-reveal] now at its correct pre-reveal opacity-0 state instead of stuck at 1.

items.title: RSC prefetch requests hit middleware catch-all, redirect cross-origin, throw a real client-side error
items.blocked_reason:
Found live on abacus-plumbing 2026-08-16 once hydration was fixed (invisible before -- Link prefetch never fires on an unhydrated page, so this bug only became observable AFTER HYDR-01). Next's client router prefetches linked routes via fetch() to paths like /services/__next._tree.txt. Those paths are not recognised by the shared lane's middleware klaudius resolver and fall through to its catch-all, which redirects to grayreserve.com -- cross-origin, so the fetch fails CORS, and that failure surfaces as an uncaught 't[Symbol.asyncIterator] is not a function' in Next's flight-stream parser. Confirmed NOT to break user-facing behaviour: with the prefetch requests blocked entirely, the mobile menu opens correctly, so this is console noise and wasted requests on every real visit, not a functional defect.
OUT OF SCOPE FROM THIS REPO: same file as OPS-05 (gr-no-website-builds/apps/previews/src/middleware.ts), same off-limits rule (klaudius/CLAUDE.md rule 1), same blast radius concern (ci.yml triggers on any push, ~80 live tenants). Likely the SAME underlying middleware gap as OPS-05's soft-404 -- both are the klaudius-lane resolver not recognising a valid-but-unusual path shape and falling through to the generic catch-all instead of a klaudius-aware 404. Worth fixing together with OPS-05, Jeff's call.

items.title: Cross-build convergence ledger (scripts/design-ledger.mjs)
items.verified:
Ported gr-no-website-builds's feelsTooClose() pattern, adapted two ways per Fable's correction of the port: (1) runs at DESIGN-CHOICE time before any TSX exists rather than post-build -- a twin caught before code is written costs one re-check; caught after, a full rebuild, which is exactly what the source pattern's own numbers show turning a 23-min build into 46; (2) compares by REGISTER not exact value -- ground hue in 30-degree bins, typography by FORMULA NUMBER (1-5) not font family name, mirroring the source's own hard-won lesson that exact-name matching is escaped by a different name in the identical visual class.
Weights: ground family + formula number DOMINANT (+2 each), hue-bin/harmony/character supporting (+1 each), threshold >=5, capped at last 40 fingerprints (oldest evicted) -- same shape as the source, sized to klaudius's own axes.
TESTED, all 4 cases: true positive (identical choices score 6, correctly TWIN); true negative (ground+formula match alone, everything else differs, scores 4, correctly CLEAR -- caught and fixed my own first test which accidentally left an extra axis matching); eviction cap holds exactly at 40 with oldest evicted on the 41st write; corrupt ledger file fails OPEN (treats as empty, never crashes the build) rather than closed.
Wired into build/SKILL.md right after the last of the 4 design decisions (ground is last in file order), with an explicit 2-forced-re-pick cap before accepting a twin with a recorded reason -- a steer, not a hard wall.

items.title: Targeted HyperUI lookup by need + cache-locality guidance — IMPLEMENTED
items.note:
Jeff's instruction 2026-08-16, explicit: 'we don't need to do that until we see if this actually works, but I want you to put it like on the notes or ledger just to be safe' -- this is a PARKED FOLLOW-UP, not a task to start now, and only becomes relevant if the experiment/hyperui-components build against thewoodlandsplumbingandair.com actually produces a genuinely better site than a non-HyperUI baseline.
THE PROBLEM, as he named it: right now a build that needs ONE accordion example has to read the whole 591-line INDEX.md (469 files across 56 categories) to find it -- linear top-to-bottom scanning regardless of what's actually needed. 'If it needs an accordion or a button or a hero style, it doesn't need to scan everything else.'
THE FIX, when/if this is picked up: a targeted lookup instead of a full-file read. Concretely, options to evaluate: (a) a small script (e.g. scripts/hyperui-lookup.mjs <category> [--tier application|marketing]) that queries index.json and returns only the matching category's entries -- e.g. `node scripts/hyperui-lookup.mjs accordions` returns just the 10 accordion entries, not the other 459; (b) split INDEX.md into one small per-category file (reference/hyperui/{category}/INDEX.md) so the build reads only the directory it needs; (c) both -- a lookup script for programmatic/deterministic access plus per-category indexes for quick human/model browsing. index.json (already built by scripts/build-hyperui-index.mjs) already has everything needed to build either without re-fetching from GitHub -- this is a query layer on top of data that already exists, not new data collection.
WHY THIS MATTERS IF THE EXPERIMENT SUCCEEDS: at 50-100 builds/day, every build re-reading a 591-line index it mostly doesn't need is real waste. CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (Fable review, token/compaction audit): the '86% output tokens' figure above was measured before the per-line-vs-per-message-id dedup bug in cost_ledger.py was fixed, and does not hold on deduped data -- output is actually ~3% of a real build's weighted cost; cache_read (context replay across ~200 turns) is ~75%. This does not change the lookup fix's value (it still cuts standing context and turn count, both real levers), but the OLD justification pointed at the wrong mechanism -- fix it because it replays every build, not because of raw output-token generation. A targeted lookup could turn 'read 591 lines to find 10' into 'read exactly 10'.
DO NOT BUILD THIS UNTIL the experiment result is known -- if HyperUI-as-reference does not measurably help, this whole item is moot and the vendored reference set + index should likely be removed rather than optimized.

EXTENDED 2026-08-16, Jeff's synthesis while the test build was mid-run: quality and efficiency are separate questions -- if the output is genuinely good, the cost problems below are all known, fixable levers, not a reason to reject the idea. Live evidence while this note was written: the test build hit 6 auto-compactions (vs 2 for the worst prior build) and 8.84M weighted tokens BEFORE finishing QA or deploying, already approaching abacus-plumbing's full FINISHED total of 9.28M -- strong signal the reference set is costing more than a disciplined implementation would.
THREE LEVERS, to apply together if/when this unblocks:
1. COMPACTION -- fixed directly by the targeted-lookup fix already specified above (less context held at once = fewer compactions).
2. CACHE LOCALITY -- a distinct lever not covered above. This project's own cost data shows cache-read tokens are 10x-discounted and normally carry most of a build's weight. If reference material is read scattered throughout a session instead of once in a stable early position, it fights Claude's own prompt cache instead of using it. Fix: whatever reference material a build needs should load ONCE, early, in one place -- not ad hoc as generation proceeds.
3. ROUTE THE LOOKUP TO ZERO COST, NOT A CHEAPER MODEL -- 'given a category name, return matching filenames' is a zero-reasoning operation; it does not need Haiku, it needs no model at all. The hyperui-lookup.mjs script above does it for literal $0 and 0 tokens, which beats even the cheapest model tier. Note this is DIFFERENT from and safer than the broader Ruflo-style pipeline-stage tiering already evaluated and REJECTED in this project (see TIER-01: Fable's finding was more model seams = more failure surface, not worth it for find/gather/build/QA). A deterministic filter over an existing JSON file is not a model seam at all, so it does not reopen that rejected question.

SHIPPED 2026-08-16, per Jeff's explicit override of the original contingency ('there's no reason for you to wait on a HyperUI fail... start injecting all those fixes... into the test branch'). Did NOT wait for the running experiment build to finish -- implemented in parallel while it was still mid-QA, on experiment/hyperui-components only, never touching main.

Lever 1 (targeted lookup) + lever 3 (zero-cost routing): scripts/hyperui-lookup.mjs <category> [--tier application|marketing] -- a deterministic filter over the existing index.json, $0 and ~0 tokens, returns only the matching category instead of the full 591-line INDEX.md. Smoke-tested: `accordions --tier application` returns exactly the 10 accordion entries; an unknown category exits 1 with a clear message; --list-categories enumerates all 56 category names.
Lever 2 (cache locality): build/SKILL.md's HyperUI section now instructs loading all reference material ONCE, early -- right after design-system/palette decisions, before any page.tsx exists -- via the lookup script for the 4-6 categories the client plausibly needs, read in one batch. Previously there was no instruction on WHEN to read reference material at all, which is exactly what let it happen ad hoc (or not at all, per the first test).

items.title: Mandatory, verifiable HyperUI adoption gate — fixes 'available but unused'
items.note:
Root cause of the first experiment test testing nothing, per direct transcript audit: the reference set was vendored and indexed, but build/SKILL.md's HyperUI section was entirely advisory ('read INDEX.md first', 'every file you actually use, without exception: do X') -- it never required using any file at all, and status.md's 'informed by' prose was allowed to substitute for real citations. A build that used zero files was fully compliant with the letter of the instructions.

SHIPPED 2026-08-16, same parallel-lane basis as HYPERUI-01 -- built while the tainted first test was still running, so the NEXT test (fresh URL, per Jeff) starts under the fixed rules from turn one.

Fix, three parts:
1. build/SKILL.md HyperUI section rewritten with a hard floor: >=4 distinct application-tier components, from >=3 distinct categories, each cited as the real structural starting point for a named element (concrete category-to-need suggestions given: accordions->FAQ, stats->review numbers, badges->licences, tabs->service categories, timelines->process, modals->lightbox/contact). Marketing-tier citations are logged but don't count toward the floor -- deliberately, so the gate can't be satisfied by leaning on the tier already proven to produce 3-4/10 stock-content sites.
2. status.md must carry a NEW, exact heading: '## HyperUI components used' (not 'references used', which is what let the first test's prose pass unnoticed), one line per component citing the exact vendored path in backticks plus what it became.
3. scripts/hyperui-usage-check.mjs <slug> -- new deterministic QA gate, wired into qa-reviewer.md's Step 3 (same pattern as verify-photos.mjs) and Step 4's hard-blocker checklist. Validates every cited path is real against index.json, enforces the 4/3 floor, and as a non-blocking secondary signal greps the shipped site source for raw HyperUI Tailwind colour classes that leaked in verbatim (should have become derived palette tokens per SKILL.md rule 1). Prints HYPERUI_USAGE_CHECK=PASS/FAIL/SKIP -- SKIP when the reference set isn't present (i.e. every branch except this one), so it can never block a normal build. Smoke-tested all 5 paths: clean PASS (4 components/4 categories), too-few/wrong-category FAIL, missing-section FAIL, fake-path FAIL, and a PASS with a colour-leak WARNING -- all produced the expected verdict.

Honesty limit stated in the script's own header: citing a real path proves the path was named and exists, not that the generated TSX truly inherited its structure. It is a floor, not proof -- but it is a materially higher bar than the zero-citation 'informed by' prose that let the first test ship with no verifiable usage at all, which is exactly what Jeff asked for: 'an honest, actual usage of hyper UI to judge against'.

STILL OPEN / not done here: the currently-running first test (the-woodlands-plumbing-and-air) is allowed to finish under the OLD rules -- per the standing 'must finish no matter the cost' instruction, it was never interrupted or restarted for this fix. Its result is being treated by Jeff as tainted/non-representative for the HyperUI question specifically (not for the design-quality-in-general question). The NEXT build, once Jeff supplies a fresh URL, is the first one that will run under HYPERUI-01+HYPERUI-02 together -- that is the honest test.

I don't see a lot of that sections library there.' Correct diagnosis: the 4-component floor only counted application-tier ATOMIC WIDGETS (accordions, badges, stats, timelines) grafted onto an otherwise 100%-custom page STRUCTURE -- the hero layout, feature grid, and CTA band never drew on the library at all. items.title: Color theory 'a bit off' — ground/secondary hue collision, now flagged (not auto-corrected)
items.note:
Jeff: 'color theory seems a bit off but it's not brown so that's good!' (confirming the earlier always-brown fix held). Investigated the real token values: ground-hue=210deg (fallback rule, correct in isolation) and split-harmony secondary=178deg (rotated off the RED accent, correct in isolation) land only 32deg apart -- both read as one muddy blue-green neutral family instead of a deliberate ground + a distinct second brand colour. Added a visibility check instead, same pattern as the existing SEMANTIC COLLISION warning: derive-palette.mjs now prints '⚠️ GROUND/SECONDARY TOO CLOSE' whenever the two hues are <60deg apart, in both console and --json output. items.title: Fable token-cost review: ledger bug fixed, 5 efficiency fixes shipped
items.note:
Dispatched a Fable-model review (in parallel with continued build-quality lifting) to find real ways to cut build 2's token cost toward Jeff's 7-8M target. Fable's finding 0 was the most important: the reported 11.77M/13.23M numbers were THEMSELVES WRONG. cost_ledger.py's session_tokens() summed every JSONL LINE, but Claude Code writes one line per content block and repeats the full usage object on each -- 540 usage lines vs 234 real API calls on build 2, inflating cache_write ~3.9x and cache_read ~2.2x. It also never scanned subagent transcripts (<session>/subagents/*.jsonl), undercounting by everything a build delegated (the QA subagent alone was another ~1.59M true-weighted, 25% of the whole build, silently dropped).

FIXED: session_tokens() now dedupes by message.id (max per field, not sum -- output_tokens specifically accumulates across a message's streamed lines) and folds in the sibling subagents/ directory. Re-measured with the corrected ledger: build 1 = 8.76M (was reported 13.23M), build 2 = 6.42M (was reported 11.77M, matches Fable's independent 6.42M exactly). Real delta: build 2 is 26.7% CHEAPER than build 1, and ALREADY inside the 7-8M target -- just never correctly measured. Corrected the earlier wrong numbers with Jeff directly.

SHIPPED, Fable's ranked low-risk fixes (skipped the two highest-effort/risk ones -- full SKILL.md core/reference split and full gate-battery script consolidation -- for a later pass, given time; the 5 below required no such tradeoff):
1. .claude/settings.json env.PATH expanded to the full set the model has been manually re-exporting on ~88% of Bash calls (a known, previously-logged emergent pattern) -- one settings fix instead of a redundant export on every call.
2. build/SKILL.md: new 'After a compaction: re-read narrow, never re-read whole' section -- a real build re-read page.tsx 5x and site-data.ts 7x across its own compactions.
3. qa-reviewer.md: on a SCOPED round only, skip re-reading template-frozen component files (Motion.tsx, HeroVideo.tsx, SiteChat.tsx, schema.ts) unless a gate implicates them or they're in the touched set -- they're byte-identical across builds.
4. deploy/SKILL.md split: the three non-Vercel provider sections (Cloudflare/Netlify/self-host, 335 of 917 lines -- 36% of the file) moved to deploy/reference/non-vercel-hosts.md, read only when DEPLOY_PROVIDER isn't vercel. This install always runs vercel, so every real deploy call now injects 591 lines instead of 917. Verified: no broken cross-references, the 'Pick the host' routing logic updated to point at the reference file.
One Fable finding checked and NOT actioned: a claimed duplicate reference/hyperui/application/ path -- verified with a repo-wide find, no such directory exists on disk; likely a stale artifact from an earlier vendoring step already cleaned up, not a real current issue.

NOT YET DONE, real remaining upside per Fable's estimate: build/SKILL.md core/reference split (~1.0-1.3M, 15-20%, the highest-value remaining lever but needs care to keep every hard floor/contract verbatim in the core) and gate-battery script consolidation (~0.6-0.9M, 10-14%, near-zero risk, just needs the scripting work). items.verified: Committed e2f0c22c (gr-no-website-builds-lane). Real root cause found (different from the prior guess): context.rewrite() re-enters Astro's OWN route table, not Vercel's static filesystem handler -- the only matching route is the catch-all pages/klaudius/[slug]/[...page].ts, whose loadKlaudiusDoc() falls back to 'home' for any unrecognized key, so the rewrite silently served the HOME PAGE at 200 (worse than the original 302). INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED (not just trusting the agent's report): curl -L .../chat-kb.json returns real JSON; a real POST to klaudius-site-chat.vercel.app/api/chat returns a KB-grounded answer (tankless water heaters, correct service area, correct phone number) -- CLOSES CHAT-04 at last.

items.title: Permanent floor-lift: gate hardening + proof-of-read hash + design-lift plan -- Fable-reviewed, implemented, verified
note: Triggered by Jeff live-reviewing the real aot-mechanical deploy and finding it visibly flat/generic despite passing gates -- his own framing: "the floor has to be permanent lifting" and "the reason we bought this is 6 months of failures with our engine, we aren't doing that again." Root cause: richness-check.mjs and hyperui-transplant-check.mjs both had WARN-only checks for exactly the defects Jeff found (gradient count <4, photo-grounded sections <2, HyperUI citations scored DECORATIVE/UNSTAMPED) -- both scripts even had their own pre-written escalation plan ("hand-inspect against a real rendered build, promote to hard FAIL if it holds"). Tonight was that hand-inspection. 2026-08-18 HARD GATE from Jeff, verbatim: "we arent running again until there is a serious design lift within the logic that stays on token count and time." No client build/deploy dispatch of any kind is authorized until: (a) Fable confirms the gate-hardening (hyperui-transplant-check.mjs, richness-check.mjs, hero-video mandate) is actually complete and correctly wired, not just claimed; (b) Fable confirms caching (node_modules reuse) and compartmentalization (concurrent-dispatch safety, the WATCH_DIR gap just closed) are solid; (c) a credible path exists to deliver the fix within the previously-measured ~6-9M token / <=90 min envelope. Also separately requested: this fix-pass dispatch (SEQ-07) was killed by Jeff before finishing, explicitly NOT to be redispatched without further instruction. SCOPE EXPANDED 2026-08-18: Jeff flagged the original Fable consult only asked for a review of already-made patches, not a design of the systemic fix itself ("you didnt mention the large design lift"). Sent a follow-up message to the same running agent (a9c17c4cbdfc4d2e3) adding: (1) whether build/SKILL.md GENERATION instructions (not just Verify gates) are weak or were bypassed under pressure -- distinguish the two; (2) whether richness/hero-video steps are ordered LAST in the build task sequence, making them the first things dropped under time pressure, and if so a reordering/checkpoint fix; (3) a real cost estimate of do-it-right-first-pass vs ship-thin-then-fix; (4) any other structural lever to make serious design lift the DEFAULT outcome, not something that only happens after an operator complains about an already-shipped site. Same output file, same final report. FABLE REVIEW COMPLETE 2026-08-18, both rounds. Round 1 found 4 real gaps in the initial hardening (gradient-floor instruction drift, missing hero-video escape hatch consideration, prose-only hero-video gate, stale WARN-language in qa-reviewer.md/transplant-check header) plus a full caching/compartmentalization audit (no npm ci, no shared node_modules cache -- 23-46 GB/day projected at target volume, prune-client-build.mjs mandated but skipped in practice on the real aot deploy, one real remaining race on data/design-fingerprints.json unlocked read-modify-write across 5 scripts) plus a design-lift strategy (move hero-video render into Setup so a kill cannot erase the attempt, a pre-TSX design-manifest checkpoint, a mid-build richness checkpoint, confirmed the do-it-right-first-pass-is-cheaper hypothesis with real numbers -- richness fixes touch globals.css/_components which are escalation triggers, so a second pass is never scoped, always a full re-review). Round 2 (after Jeff asked for the actual hyperUI citations to be checked): Fable ran the promoted gate against aot-mechanical live output for real -- 7 of 15 citations DECORATIVE, 1 uncited stamp, confirmed HYPERUI_TRANSPLANT_CHECK=FAIL on this exact build. Root-caused WHY: build/SKILL.md own example citation block listed 6 real vendored paths and this build cited 4 of them verbatim including the two proven-bogus ones -- rules-lose-to-examples, the documented standing failure mode, playing out exactly. Proposed the proof-of-read hash as the real fix.

Dead WARN-exit tail removed. node --check passes. 2) richness-check.mjs: gradient-count<4 and photo-grounded-sections<2 moved from warnings.push to failures.push (result becomes FAIL, not just noted). node --check passes. 3) build/SKILL.md SS Motion, chat and hero video: hero-video render step marked MANDATORY ATTEMPT (was previously fully skippable with no record -- "a failure here is not a build failure" language had no counterpart gate, so a build could skip the render call ENTIRELY, not just fail it, and nothing would ever know).
